text: Working with APIs is an essential skill for modern developers. An API allows your program to communicate with another service by sending HTTP requests, such as GET or POST, to a specific URL. Most APIs return data in JSON format, which is easy to read and parse. Before you can access the data, you usually need authentication, for example an API key or a token, to prove your identity. It is also important to respect rate limits, which restrict how many requests you can make within a certain time. Finally, good error handling helps you deal with problems like missing data or server failures, so your application stays stable and reliable.
